11.name: GND

WCH recommends the CH224A for CH224K designs (note under 6.2 p. 9; table 3-1 note 2 p. 2); the CH224A differs: pin 1 VHV rated 32 V, internal pull-ups on CFG2 and CFG3, CFG1 rated 3.8 V, VBUS 32 V, other configuration values (7.1, 7.3 p. 11–12)
over-temperature protection threshold 90 / 105 / 120 °C; power-on reset 2.2 / 2.4 / 2.6 V (8.2.3 p. 14)

checked: ESSOP10 pinout p. 2 and table 4-2 p. 3 = EasyEDA symbol of C970725 (1 VDD … 10 PG, 11 GND = exposed pad)
absolute maximum 8.1.3 p. 13 and electrical parameters 8.2.3 p. 14 of the CH224K
reference schematic 6.2 p. 9: 1 kΩ VBUS → VDD, 1 µF at VDD, 10 kΩ VBUS → pin 8, I/O-level table 5–20 V

2026-10-31 (schema W5, read again): VDD shunt regulator VLDOK 3.24 / 3.3 / 3.36 V, sinking ILDO 0 … 30 mA (8.2.3 p. 14) – values vdd_shunt_v, i_shunt_max_a, behaviour pd_sink; the CH224K's request by I/O levels (reference 6.2 p. 9): CFG1 = 1 → 5 V; CFG1 = 0 with CFG2 CFG3 = 00 → 9 V, 01 → 12 V, 11 → 15 V, 10 → 20 V – values pd_request_v (table 5-2 p. 5 is the CH224Q/A's, with other voltages)
open: not in stock at LCSC or JLCPCB (2026-10-31); WCH recommends the CH224A – it would need its own entry (other ratings and configuration values)
pin 8 (VBUS sense) is rated 13.5 V, the reference requests up to 20 V through 10 kΩ; the data sheet says nothing about an internal clamp – the simulation without a model shows VBUS at the pin
the absolute-maximum table gives VDD as 3.0 … 3.6 V (a minimum of 3.0 V in an absolute-maximum table)
DP, DM, CFG2, CFG3 absolute maxima are relative to VDD (VDD + 0.5 V); PG has no absolute maximum for the CH224K
no input thresholds for CFG1–CFG3, no supply current and no θJA or junction limit for the CH224K
single-resistor configuration values of the CH224K are not in version 2.1 (table 5-1 is for CH224Q/CH224A, and 7.3 says the values differ)
the series resistors at VDD and pin 8 are entered as pull_up (a resistor to the VBUS supply net) without a window; the sink limit 30 mA bounds the VDD resistor from below for the highest VBUS
behaviour pd_sink models the VDD shunt only; PG, the CC lines and the request on the CC wire are not simulated – the charger is the project's source in sim.json at the voltage it delivers
